items.summary: Unrefereed research candidate. A wide binary star takes thousands of years to complete one orbit, so its eccentricity usually cannot be found by following the orbit. Astronomers instead use the angle Γ between the pair's projected separation and projected relative velocity, whose distribution over many binaries depends on the population's eccentricity law. Hwang, Ting and Zakamska (MNRAS 2022, Appendix B) asked whether this angle distribution determines the eccentricity distribution uniquely. In the ideal model (random orbital phase, uniformly random 3D orientation, error-free projections) this package derives the likelihood of one angle in closed form, p(γ|e) = [acosh(1/e) − 1{|cos γ| > e} acosh(|cos γ|/e)] / (π sin²γ), and shows that its mixtures are classical Abel transforms. This gives an explicit inverse for every eccentricity law, including atoms: different eccentricity laws never give the same angle law. The inverse is continuous in the weak topology but discontinuous in total variation, so fine structure can be nearly invisible. Moments need no inversion: E√(1−e²) = (π/2) E sin³Γ and E e² = 1/2 + E cos 2Γ − (1/2) E cos 4Γ; these are the only symmetric unbiased single-angle observables for their targets and give near-efficient power-law index estimators. Two exact selection results bear on Gaia samples: thermal populations keep a uniform angle law under selections that ignore sky position angles, and binning by projected separation preserves the model under a log-uniform semimajor-axis law. The archive contains the 21-page manuscript (PDF and LaTeX source) with complete proofs, a Python library (likelihoods, observables, estimators, Kepler simulators), the full validation script with recorded results and figures, semantic negative controls, fast CI checks, the bounded novelty report and SHA-256 sums. All data are synthetic; no observational catalogue is analysed. Assurance boundary: written proofs; floating-point numerical checks and Kepler simulations; producer-side replay in normal and optimised modes; internal AI-assisted review (five roles, adversarial correctness review, proof audit and re-review). This is not peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification. Creator: Anonymous. Prose, manuscript and data CC0-1.0; code MIT.

items.summary: This Version 2.1 report places the Maxwell Mass Effect at the forefront of a coherent model for the Venusian atmosphere. The surface temperature is treated as the dependent variable required to support the atmospheric mass against gravity. Solar energy is captured in a shallow topside thermal heating pool, stored as potential energy, and returned to depth by organised descent in the polar vortices under conservation of angular momentum. The sulfuric-acid lifting condensation level (LCL) acts as the thermodynamic anchor (Dew-Point Anchor Hypothesis). A two-component radiative opacity lapse rate then fixes only the geometric separation between that LCL and the infrared emission level. Stochastic inverse modelling with a VIRA equatorial profile, hydrostatic integration and thermodynamic filters recovers a cloud base near 49.6 km, an emission level near 69.4 km at approximately 229 K, and a surface pressure of approximately 91.5 bar. An order-of-magnitude energy-budget test shows that the required polar mass flux lies within the range of observed vortex descent speeds. Version 2 adds a quantitative recirculation (recycle) test using existing Venusian meridional circulation wind data. Observed poleward flows of ~10–15 m s⁻¹ at cloud tops imply a hemispheric Hadley-cell mass flux of order 10¹¹ kg s⁻¹ and a full recirculation timescale of 1–2 weeks. This multi-cycle pathway resolves the apparent single-pass temperature-rise tension and brings the adiabatic signature into agreement with observed polar temperature contrasts of 15–50 K. The same boundary conditions can be satisfied by a conventional greenhouse calculation, but only the Maxwell framework supplies a structural explanation for the polar vortices themselves and a dynamically consistent energy pathway. A new Discussion section explains the changes from Version 1 and how they address independent criticisms of the energy-budget magnitude and the need for a discriminating quantitative test. Diagnostic figures from the inverse model and the recirculation test are included.

items.summary: The magnetotelluric (MT) method uses natural electromagnetic field variations to image subsurface electrical resistivity at depths ranging from tens of metres to hundreds of kilometres. It is widely used in geophysical exploration for natural resources, including minerals, geothermal energy, and groundwater, as well as in the characterisation of sites for CO$_2$ storage and in studies of crustal and lithospheric structure. The MT inverse problem is, however, inherently non-unique: many distinct resistivity models reproduce the observations equally well. Conventional practice nonetheless reports a single regularised model, with no quantitative measure of its uncertainty. MTGeophysics.jl is a Julia package developed to address this limitation. Its principal aim is the quantification of uncertainty in MT model building, advancing interpretation from a single deterministic model, through an ensemble of plausible models, towards the full posterior distribution. The package also provides tools for data analysis, mesh generation, masking, forward modelling, inversion, model analysis and visualisation for MT research and applications. items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents embedded in software-as-a-service (SaaS) platforms inherit the user's permissions. When a permission is revoked during a task, the platform rejects the next read, but the agent still retains the data it previously retrieved in its context, drafts, saved documents, and memory. This study examined how platforms can enforce a mid-task revocation on that working state. The author defined correct behavior for four revocation types, each mapped to an obligation to block, purge, or suspend, including leaks through paraphrases, aggregates, and existence hints. The author built RevBench, a simulated field-service platform, and compared nine enforcement designs from access control, information-flow control, and machine unlearning on six frontier models in 6,048 runs. Outputs were scored using exact matching and two large-language-model judges. Per-call authorization still failed in 417 of 720 runs (57.9%), rising from 34.4% when the revocation preceded retrieval to 72.8% when it followed delivery. Information-flow labels leaked the least (12.9%) but left revoked data saved in 44.2% of runs. Designs that invalidated the context performed best, while editing the context in place left derived facts behind. A full restart and selective replay with listing-level provenance reached 21.4% and 21.0% substantive failure, the latter with 12.1% fewer model calls. Most remaining failures were disclosures about the restriction, often repeating the platform’s own notice, and larger models did not reduce them. SaaS platforms need revocation controls that reach the agent’s working state and match the type of revocation. items.summary: Learned surrogates of process simulators are often evaluated on random states from plants they have already seen. This technical report compares interpolation, leave-one-case-out, and leave-one-ore-group-out evaluation for five models trained on a steady-state mineral-processing simulator. The simulator tracks mineral mass over 63 size classes, water, closed grinding circuits, and unit-level balance closure. It reports limitations against published examples alongside the comparisons. On a 3,072-state design over twelve authored cases, the multilayer perceptron gives the lowest interpolation recovery RMSE (3.38 percentage points), but has a 26.24-point mean RMSE when each case is held out. The Gaussian process has the lowest mean held-out-case RMSE (10.95 points), while the perceptron has the highest median case-fold R-squared (0.547). Under ore-group holdout, the perceptron's median recovery R-squared is 0.437 across seven groups, but varies from 0.795 for the five chalcopyrite cases to -10.2 for the two gold-in-pyrite cases. Log-upgrade transfer is poor for every model. The cases are authored; these results do not establish performance on operating plants. The report documents the mineral-processing simulator, its physical models, machine-learning evaluation methods, a process-specific optimization study, data and preprocessing, validation protocols, limitations, and reproducibility. Source code and computational records: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_OreFlow

items.summary: This repository provides the MATLAB source code and reproducibility resources associated with the manuscript entitled “Physics-Guided Reduced-Order Screening of Radiative Loss, Preferential Diffusion, and NOₓ Pathway Competition in Ammonia/Hydrogen Diffusion Flames,” submitted to the International Journal of Hydrogen Energy (Manuscript No. HE-D-26-13275). The computational framework employs a two-dimensional axisymmetric, physics-guided reduced-order model to investigate the coupled effects of radiative heat loss, preferential diffusion, ammonia cracking, hydrogen enrichment, pressure, and strain on non-premixed ammonia/hydrogen diffusion flames. The MATLAB implementation supports the reproduction of the manuscript's numerical analyses, including baseline flame characteristics, reaction-zone localization, thermal response, relative NOₓ formation tendencies, scalar dissipation, extinction susceptibility, robustness indicators, mechanism-isolation studies, numerical convergence, closure sensitivity, uncertainty analyses, parametric sweeps, and Pareto-based screening. Repository contents and reproducibility The principal file, Master_NH3H2_ROM_Reproducibility.m , contains the model formulation, numerical procedures, analysis modules, and routines for generating supporting figures, numerical tables, and datasets. Executing the master function creates an organized output directory containing the enabled computational results. Model scope and limitations The framework is intended for comparative mechanism screening and prioritization of operating conditions for subsequent higher-fidelity investigations. It does not solve the full governing conservation equations or detailed chemical kinetics. The relative NOₓ formation-tendency index is not an absolute emission concentration, emission factor, or outlet flux. Similarly, the extinction and robustness indicators represent comparative screening metrics rather than experimentally validated stability limits. The repository supports transparency, reproducibility, and further development of computational screening methods for ammonia/hydrogen combustion. Associated manuscript: International Journal of Hydrogen Energy, HE-D-26-13275. Keywords: Ammonia/hydrogen combustion; reduced-order modeling; MATLAB; radiative heat loss; preferential diffusion; NOₓ formation tendency; extinction; uncertainty analysis; reproducibility.

items.summary: A phase-only spatial light modulator in the pupil of a microscope objective can form hundreds to thousands of optical traps at once, but only if the phase pattern it displays is computed well: the pattern fixes how much light reaches the traps, how equal the traps are, where stray light goes, how the pattern survives a real device, and how fast it can be recomputed when traps move. DinHot is an open studio that runs 24 methods (19 published ones and 5 proposed here) on the same task, with the same seeds, metrics and device model, in Python as the reference and in a TypeScript port that runs live in a browser. We describe the optical and device model, the methods with the measured acceptance of each, 14 cases from a 3 x 3 array to a disordered 819-trap array and shaped potentials, the benchmark protocol, two learned models, and the 5 proposed methods, three of which meet their acceptance criteria on their acceptance tasks, each within a scope that the benchmark or the scope measurements narrow (a device-aware weighted Gerchberg-Saxton update, a flicker-bounded phase-continuous sequence and an efficiency-uniformity front), one of which meets a narrowed criterion (an aberration-robust hologram) and one of which is refuted by measurement (a learned warm start for phase-fixed weighted GS). A network trained on three-plane volumes beats its baseline at equal wall-clock on all 162 held-out volumes (median accuracy ratio 1.140), whereas its two-dimensional counterpart ties with Gerchberg-Saxton (ratio 0.9994). The model is a scalar Fourier model of a simulated device, not a calibrated instrument. Interactive studio and reproducible pipeline (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CEFOP_DinHot . Interactive studio: https://dinhot.fasl-work.com .

items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents embedded in software-as-a-service (SaaS) platforms inherit the user's permissions. When a permission is revoked during a task, the platform rejects the next read, but the agent still retains the data it previously retrieved in its context, drafts, saved documents, and memory. This study examined how platforms can enforce a mid-task revocation on that working state. The author defined correct behavior for four revocation types, each mapped to an obligation to block, purge, or suspend, including leaks through paraphrases, aggregates, and existence hints. The author built RevBench, a simulated field-service platform, and compared nine enforcement designs from access control, information-flow control, and machine unlearning on six frontier models in 6,048 runs. Outputs were scored using exact matching and two large-language-model judges. Per-call authorization still failed in 417 of 720 runs (57.9%), rising from 34.4% when the revocation preceded retrieval to 72.8% when it followed delivery. Information-flow labels leaked the least (12.9%) but left revoked data saved in 44.2% of runs. Designs that invalidated the context performed best, while editing the context in place left derived facts behind. A full restart and selective replay with listing-level provenance reached 21.4% and 21.0% substantive failure, the latter with 12.1% fewer model calls. Most remaining failures were disclosures about the restriction, often repeating the platform’s own notice, and larger models did not reduce them. SaaS platforms need revocation controls that reach the agent’s working state and match the type of revocation. items.summary: Phase-fixed weighted Gerchberg-Saxton (WGS) is the practical method for large arrays of optical traps, but it optimizes the hologram on an ideal model of the spatial light modulator (SLM), and the sequences that move traps interpolate between holograms that were never optimized for the frames in between. We test two hypotheses against the strongest baselines on the same scalar Fourier model. First, keeping the WGS weights but replacing the phase update by conjugate-gradient steps through the pixel-crosstalk kernel and the phase quantizer of the device (device-aware WGS) lowers the trap-intensity spread on the device. On a 10 x 10 lattice behind a crosstalk device, the relative standard deviation falls from a median of 5.21 percent for phase-fixed WGS at 30 iterations (5.21 percent at 100) to 0.205 percent, a median factor of 26 over 5 seeds (range 16 to 33) at a median 0.995 of the baseline's efficiency; the factor is 7.9 with 4-bit phase and a fill factor of 0.85 added, and 2.0 on a smaller 8 x 8 grid with flicker added and a fixed 30-iteration budget (the ratio of the means of 3 seeds); over the 5 geometries of the studio's benchmark on that device the median factor is 1.73 (0.97 to 4.69), and 2 of them meet both thresholds. A control that removes the device model from the loop gains nothing (5.14 percent), so the gain comes from the model. Second, optimizing every intermediate hologram of a moving-trap sequence with the trap phases locked to a smooth trajectory (flicker-bounded sequence) keeps the minimum transient intensity of the moving traps at a median 0.920 of their mean (range 0.915 to 0.932) over 5 seeds at 13 frames (below 0.9 at seven frames), against 0.654 (0.551 to 0.709) for linear phase interpolation. On longer moves, with the frames that keep the peak step per frame at most 0.2 Fourier units, the bound is met on 6 and 6 of 8 seeds of two lattice moves and on 5 of 6 seeds of a rearrangement case; the seeds that miss it miss it on the phase path their end phases prescribe, and at an equal number of frames on the rearrangement linear phase interpolation leads. Both results hold in a model of a simulated device and in a transient model that we define; neither is a hardware measurement. items.summary: Titolo: USAI-AGI: A Hybrid Cognitive Architecture for Artificial General Intelligence based on Applied Category Theory This work has been developed with the support of artificial intelligence linguistic models (Large Language Models), used as tools for consultation, exploration and co-elaboration. Every conceptual choice, every critical synthesis and every direction taken in solving the problem are the result of my autonomous thinking and my intellectual responsibility. The use of AI has represented an extension of my skills, not a substitute for my human contribution. Keywords:  Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), Cognitive Architecture, Applied Category Theory, Knowledge Representation, RDF, AI Safety, Symbolic AI, Causal Inference, Continual Learning. Description: A Hybrid, Category-Theoretic Framework for Artificial General Intelligence: Architecture for Continuous Learning, Causal Reasoning, and Self-Improvement Author:  Luigi Usai Abstract: Current advancements in artificial intelligence, particularly Large Language Models, demonstrate impressive generative capabilities but often lack robust mechanisms for persistent knowledge integration, causal reasoning, and autonomous, goal-directed behavior. This paper presents a novel, hybrid architecture for Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) that addresses these limitations by integrating symbolic reasoning, sub-symbolic pattern recognition, and a sophisticated cognitive control loop. The system's core is a probabilistic Knowledge Base (KB) built on RDF, where each fact is associated with a confidence score that evolves over time. A key contribution of this framework is its use of Applied Category Theory as a primary learning mechanism; perceptions are structured into a "Category of Perceptions," and learned concepts form a "Category of Concepts," with functors mapping between them to represent abstract patterns. Higher-order cognition is achieved through the analysis of natural transformations between these functors, enabling meta-learning and analogical reasoning. The AGI's autonomy is driven by an intrinsic motivational system based on cognitive drives such as curiosity and knowledge coherence, which guide a symbolic planner. To ensure robust world models, the system employs an Active Causal Inference module that identifies weak causal links in its KB, designs, and executes experiments to test them. Furthermore, the architecture features a powerful self-improvement mechanism, capable of analyzing its own source code, generating optimized versions via an integrated LLM (DeepSeek), and validating them through an automated testing framework. A case study in the domain of chess demonstrates the system's ability to develop and utilize a novel, non-textual chromatic language (ColorZip) for visual reasoning and strategic analysis. This hybrid approach, combining a formal mathematical foundation with generative capabilities and cognitive control, offers a structured and transparent pathway toward more adaptable, resilient, and truly general artificial intelligence. items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents embedded in software-as-a-service (SaaS) platforms inherit the user's permissions. When a permission is revoked during a task, the platform rejects the next read, but the agent still retains the data it previously retrieved in its context, drafts, saved documents, and memory. This study examined how platforms can enforce a mid-task revocation on that working state. The author defined correct behavior for four revocation types, each mapped to an obligation to block, purge, or suspend, including leaks through paraphrases, aggregates, and existence hints. The author built RevBench, a simulated field-service platform, and compared nine enforcement designs from access control, information-flow control, and machine unlearning on six frontier models in 6,048 runs. Outputs were scored using exact matching and two large-language-model judges. Per-call authorization still failed in 417 of 720 runs (57.9%), rising from 34.4% when the revocation preceded retrieval to 72.8% when it followed delivery. Information-flow labels leaked the least (12.9%) but left revoked data saved in 44.2% of runs. Designs that invalidated the context performed best, while editing the context in place left derived facts behind. A full restart and selective replay with listing-level provenance reached 21.4% and 21.0% substantive failure, the latter with 12.1% fewer model calls. Most remaining failures were disclosures about the restriction, often repeating the platform’s own notice, and larger models did not reduce them. SaaS platforms need revocation controls that reach the agent’s working state and match the type of revocation. items.summary: Code and results for the paper "Leakage-Aware, Edge-Deployable Brain Tumor MRI Classification: A Latency, Accuracy and Calibration Benchmark". Motivation: Ashwini et al. (doi:10.1155/acis/2622873) note that most current brain tumor segmentation and classification methods rely on offline, static imaging and therefore do not support real-time monitoring. That paper reports results on the Kaggle Brain Tumor MRI dataset (7,023 scans: pituitary, glioma, meningioma and no tumor). This record addresses part of that gap by measuring per-image CPU latency of four classifiers, as a proxy for real-time capability, and by checking whether duplicate images inflate reported accuracy. Contents: a pipeline that audits the dataset for exact and near-duplicate images, builds naive and leakage-aware splits, fine-tunes MobileNetV3, EfficientNet-B0, ResNet50 and Inception-ResNet-v2 over three seeds, measures batch-1 CPU latency, and evaluates calibration. Folders: results (main 24 runs; 7,215 images, duplicate distance 0) and results_laptop (reduced MobileNetV3 runs; 7,200 images, duplicate distance 1). The MRI images are not included; the dataset is on Kaggle (doi:10.34740/KAGGLE/DSV/2645886). See README.md for the run order.

items.summary: Data and code for Mapping bioimage-analysis software adoption in microscopy. The registry contains 33 entries: 23 analysis packages, six microscope-control programs, MATLAB and Jupyter notebooks as references, Adobe Photoshop for figure preparation and NIH Image for historical counts. The 29-package aggregate combines the 23 analysis packages with six microscope-control programs. References, Photoshop and NIH Image are excluded. After about 2000, many "NIH Image" mentions refer to ImageJ. The deep-learning series uses 13 core analysis packages. Jupyter notebooks retain their aliases, notebook category and core scope. The original 14-package calibration sample remains frozen, and the three new-package precision samples are stored separately. The archive holds processed counts, annotator-labelled validation sets, identifier-only sampling frames, configuration, code and provenance. Data sources: Europe PMC (search API and open-access full text; metadata derived from MEDLINE/PubMed carries the NLM notice that the data may not be current and that NLM does not endorse this work; full text was mined and never redistributed), OpenAlex (CC0), the GitHub REST API (public repository counts), pypistats.org (30-day PyPI download totals from the Python Software Foundation's PyPI BigQuery dataset, CC BY 4.0), the image.sc forum (topic counts only, no posts), Crossref and ORCID (bibliographic metadata, CC0), and MeSH headings from MEDLINE records (2026 MeSH vocabulary, retrieved 15 October 2026). The archive contains no article titles, abstracts or full text. Article text can be rebuilt from identifiers with release/refetch_identifiers.py through Europe PMC.
